verdict.rationale: LM Studio documents its own OpenAI-like endpoints, a REST API, and a headless daemon (llmster) that can act as a local inference backend for apps and tools, and community users confirm the OpenAI-compatible server is easy to use from real tools. However, nothing in the evidence shows a coding agent actually being connected, or documents tool-calling support that such agents need. missing for 10: documented integration with a named coding agent, tool/function-calling support on the API, hands-on reports of a coding agent running against LM Studio as its backend.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: Serve local models on OpenAI-like endpoints, locally and on the network
enables you to leverage LM Studio's technology (completions, chat completions, embedding, structured outputs via `llama.cpp` or `Apple MLX`) as local server powering your app.
LM Studio provides a REST API that you can use to interact with your local models from your own apps and scripts.
The headless LM Studio flow is especially nice because it makes local inference usable from real tools instead of as a demo.
the OpenAI server makes it really easy to spin up a server and test
